notice.line.label.description: How a notice names the line or lines it is about, by TfL's mode. `lines` is their names, joined with commas ("Northern", "333, 415"), and `count` how many. A Tube line's name comes without "line".
notice.line.label.en: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {Bus {lines}} other {Buses {lines}}}} tube {{lines} line} other {{lines}}}
notice.line.label.nb: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {Buss {lines}} other {Buss {lines}}}} tube {{lines}-linjen} other {{lines}}}

notice.line.status.description: What is wrong on a line, in a word or two, for a notice's title. `status` is the key for TfL's status: suspended (Suspended), part_suspended (Part Suspended), severe_delays (Severe Delays), issues (Issues Reported), closed (Closed, Planned Closure), part_closed (Part Closure), not_running (Not Running).
notice.line.status.en: {status, select, suspended {Suspended} part_suspended {Part suspended} severe_delays {Severe delays} issues {Issues} closed {Closed} part_closed {Part closed} not_running {Not running} other {Disrupted}}
notice.line.status.nb: {status, select, suspended {Innstilt} part_suspended {Delvis innstilt} severe_delays {Store forsinkelser} issues {Problemer} closed {Stengt} part_closed {Delvis stengt} not_running {Kjører ikke} other {Avvik}}

notice.line.title.description: The title of a line's notice: `label` is notice.line.label's, `status` notice.line.status's ("Northern line: Severe delays"). Its summary is the provider's own text, shortened.

notice.line.tag.description: The tag in front of a line's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen): a bus route's (`mode` bus, `count` 1, `line` its number), several routes with one notice (`mode` bus, `count` more), or any other line's own name.
notice.line.tag.en: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {Bus {line}} other {Buses}}} other {{line}}}
notice.line.tag.nb: {mode, select, bus {{count, plural, one {{line}-bussen} other {Busser}}} other {{line}}}

notice.weather.title.description: The title of a weather warning's notice. Its summary is notice.weather.warning's, and when it applies.

notice.weather.warning.description: A weather warning in a few words: `colour` is its level (red, amber or yellow, the Met Office's) and `hazard` what it warns of, in lower case ("wind", "rain").
notice.weather.warning.en: {colour, select, red {Red warning: {hazard}} amber {Amber warning: {hazard}} yellow {Yellow warning: {hazard}} other {Warning: {hazard}}}
notice.weather.warning.nb: {colour, select, red {Rødt farevarsel: {hazard}} amber {Oransje farevarsel: {hazard}} yellow {Gult farevarsel: {hazard}} other {Farevarsel: {hazard}}}

notice.until.description: Until when something applies, after what it is ("Amber warning: wind until Fri 21:00"). `when` is a time, a day, or a day and a time, already formatted.

notice.holiday.title.description: The title of the notice for the next bank holiday. Its summary is notice.holiday.summary's.

notice.holiday.tag.description: The tag in front of a bank holiday's notice where a notice is one line (an e-paper screen).

notice.holiday.summary.description: The next bank holiday under its title: `when` is notice.day.today's, notice.day.tomorrow's or its date, `name` the holiday's own ("Fri 25 Dec – Christmas Day").

notice.holiday.text.description: The next bank holiday in one line, after notice.holiday.tag: `when` and `name` as notice.holiday.summary's ("Tomorrow: Christmas Day").

notice.holiday.text_with_notes.description: notice.holiday.text for a holiday GOV.UK has a note on: `notes` is the note, in lower case ("Today: Boxing Day (substitute day)").

notice.day.today.description: The day something is on, when it's today; starts a line.

notice.day.tomorrow.description: The day something is on, when it's tomorrow; starts a line.
